therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: lipid-induced glucolipotoxicity and glucose-induced beta-cell stress
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: beta-cell exhaustion vs. desensitization in hyperglycemia
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: obese African Americans with history of hyperglycemic crises, including ketosis-prone and ketosis-resistant type 2 diabetes, and non-diabetic controls
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: First-Phase Insulin Release (FPIR) measured before and after 20-hour glucose infusion

results.effect_size: FPIR before glucose infusion: KPD 264, KRD 339, controls 197 µU/mL; after glucose infusion: KPD 359, KRD 381, controls 299 µU/mL
results.target_engagement_evidence: All groups showed increased FPIR after glucose infusion, indicating beta-cell responsiveness was preserved
biomarker_changes: FPIR increased in all groups after 20-hour glucose infusion
Ketosis-prone diabetics: FPIR rose from 264 to 359 µU/mL
Ketosis-resistant diabetics: FPIR rose from 339 to 381 µU/mL
Non-diabetic controls: FPIR rose from 197 to 299 µU/mL
subgroup_findings: No participants in any group experienced beta-cell failure at hour 20
Original analysis comparing beta-cell exhaustion vs. desensitization could not be performed due to absence of beta-cell failure events

dose_info.dose: Intralipid 20% at 40 mL/hr; 10% dextrose at 200 mg/m²/min

context.indication: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus with history of hyperglycemic crises in obese African Americans
context.comparator: Non-diabetic control group receiving glucose infusion
context.investigator_commentary: No participants experienced beta-cell failure, so the original analysis comparing beta-cell exhaustion versus desensitization could not be performed. All groups showed preserved and increased FPIR after glucose infusion.

modulation_entries.hypothesis: Intralipid-induced lipotoxicity was hypothesized to amplify glucose-induced beta-cell stress and precipitate beta-cell failure, but no beta-cell failure was observed in any participant
modulation_entries.citation: This study aimed to evaluate whether hyperglycemia-induced reduced beta-cell failure was the result of beta-cell exhaustion or beta-cell desensitization, however, no participants experienced beta-cell failure so this original analysis could not be performed.
